column1: Two scientists consider the origins of discoveries and other innovative behavior
column2: 两位科学家探讨科学发现及其他创新行为的起源。

column1: Scientific discovery is popularly believed to result from the sheer genius of such intellectual stars as naturalist Charles Darwin and theoretical physicist Albert Einstein.
column2: 人们普遍认为，科学发现全靠博物学家查尔斯·达尔文、理论物理学家阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦等思想巨擘的非凡才智。
column7: intellectual stars|思想界的杰出人物

column1: Our view of such unique contributions to science often disregards the person’s prior experience and the efforts of their lesser-known predecessors.
column2: 看待这种独特的科学贡献时，我们常常忽略了发现者先前的经历和那些较不知名的前辈付出的努力。

column1: Conventional wisdom also places great weight on insight in promoting breakthrough scientific achievements, as if ideas spontaneously pop into someone’s head – fully formed and functional.
column2: 传统观点也很看重灵感对突破性科学成就的推动作用，仿佛想法会自然而然地跃入某个人的脑海，一出现便已完整成形、可以付诸使用。
column4: places great weight on|十分重视
column10: functional|adj. 能实际发挥作用的

column1: There may be some limited truth to this view.
column2: 这种看法也许多少有些道理。

column1: However, we believe that it largely misrepresents the real nature of scientific discovery, as well as that of creativity and innovation in many other realms of human endeavor.
column2: 然而，我们认为，这种看法在很大程度上歪曲了科学发现的真正本质，也歪曲了人类在其他许多活动领域中进行创造和创新的本质。
column9: human endeavor|人类的活动与努力

column1: Setting aside such greats as Darwin and Einstein – whose monumental contributions are duly celebrated – we suggest that innovation is more a process of trial and error, where two steps forward may sometimes come with one step back, as well as one or more steps to the right or left.
column2: 达尔文和爱因斯坦等伟人的巨大贡献理当受到赞颂。姑且将他们放在一旁，我们认为，创新更像一个试错过程。向前走两步，有时也要后退一步，还可能向左或向右跨出一步乃至几步。

column1: This evolutionary view of human innovation undermines the notion of creative genius and recognizes the cumulative nature of scientific progress.
column2: 这种从演化角度看待人类创新的观点，动摇了所谓“创造天才”的观念，也承认科学进步具有累积性。

column1: Consider one unheralded scientist: John Nicholson, a mathematical physicist working in the 1910s who postulated the existence of ‘proto-elements’ in outer space.
column2: 以一位鲜为人知的科学家为例。数理物理学家约翰·尼科尔森在20世纪10年代从事研究，他提出外层空间存在“原始元素”的假说。

column1: By combining different numbers of weights of these proto-elements’ atoms, Nicholson could recover the weights of all the elements in the then-known periodic table.
column2: 尼科尔森按不同数量组合这些原始元素的原子量，就能算出当时元素周期表中所有已知元素的原子量。
column4: weights|n. 重量；此处指原子量

column1: These successes are all the more noteworthy given the fact that Nicholson was wrong about the presence of proto-elements: they do not actually exist.
column2: 这些成果更值得注意，因为尼科尔森对原始元素存在与否的判断是错的：它们其实并不存在。
column5: given the fact that|鉴于……这一事实

column1: Yet, amid his often fanciful theories and wild speculations, Nicholson also proposed a novel theory about the structure of atoms.
column2: 不过，在他那些往往充满幻想的理论和大胆的猜测中，尼科尔森也曾就原子结构提出一个新理论。
column4: fanciful|adj. 想象出来的；不切实际的

column1: Niels Bohr, the Nobel prize-winning father of modern atomic theory, jumped off from this interesting idea to conceive his now-famous model of the atom.
column2: 现代原子理论之父、诺贝尔奖得主尼尔斯·玻尔正是以这个有趣的想法为起点，构想出了如今著名的原子模型。
column3: Nobel prize-winning|adj. 获得诺贝尔奖的
column8: model of the atom|原子模型

column1: What are we to make of this story?
column2: 我们该如何理解这个故事呢？

column1: One might simply conclude that science is a collective and cumulative enterprise.
column2: 人们或许只会得出一个结论：科学是众人协作、逐步积累的事业。

column1: That may be true, but there may be a deeper insight to be gleaned.
column2: 这话也许没错，但从中或许还能得到更深一层的启示。

column1: We propose that science is constantly evolving, much as species of animals do.
column2: 我们提出，科学像动物物种一样，在不断演化。

column1: In biological systems, organisms may display new characteristics that result from random genetic mutations.
column2: 在生物系统中，生物体可能会呈现由随机基因突变引起的新特征。

column1: In the same way, random, arbitrary or accidental mutations of ideas may help pave the way for advances in science.
column2: 同样，想法发生的随机、任意或偶然的“变异”，可能为科学进步铺平道路。
column8: pave the way for|为……铺平道路

column1: If mutations prove beneficial, then the animal or the scientific theory will continue to thrive and perhaps reproduce.
column2: 如果这种变异证明是有益的，动物或科学理论就会继续发展壮大，甚至可能繁衍延续。

column1: Support for this evolutionary view of behavioral innovation comes from many domains.
column2: 许多领域都为这种用演化解释行为创新的观点提供了支持。

column1: Consider one example of an influential innovation in US horseracing.
column2: 以美国赛马运动中一项影响深远的创新为例。

column1: The so-called ‘acey-deucy’ stirrup placement, in which the rider’s foot in his left stirrup is placed as much as 25 centimeters lower than the right, is believed to confer important speed advantages when turning on oval tracks.
column2: 有一种称作 acey-deucy 的长短镫骑法，骑手踩在左镫上的脚最多比右脚低25厘米。据认为，这种安排能让骑手在椭圆跑道上转弯时获得重要的速度优势。

column1: It was developed by a relatively unknown jockey named Jackie Westrope.
column2: 这种骑法出自一位并不太知名的赛马骑师，他叫杰基·韦斯特罗普。

column1: Had Westrope conducted methodical investigations or examined extensive film records in a shrewd plan to outrun his rivals?
column2: 韦斯特罗普是否为了巧妙地跑赢对手，开展过系统调查，或仔细看过大量影像记录？
column4: methodical|adj. 有条不紊的；系统的

column1: Had he foreseen the speed advantage that would be conferred by riding acey-deucy?
column2: 他是否事先预见到长短镫骑法能带来速度优势？

column1: No.
column2: 没有。

column1: He suffered a leg injury, which left him unable to fully bend his left knee.
column2: 他曾腿部受伤，以致左膝无法完全弯曲。

column1: His modification just happened to coincide with enhanced left-hand turning performance.
column2: 他对骑法作出的调整，恰好改善了向左转弯的表现。

column1: This led to the rapid and widespread adoption of riding acey-deucy by many riders, a racing style which continues in today’s thoroughbred racing.
column2: 这使得长短镫骑法很快被众多骑手广泛采用，如今的纯种马比赛中仍然沿用这种赛马方式。

column1: Plenty of other stories show that fresh advances can arise from error, misadventure, and also pure serendipity – a happy accident.
column2: 还有许多故事说明，新的进展可能来自错误、不幸的意外，也可能纯属机缘巧合——一次幸运的偶然。
column8: a happy accident|一次幸运的偶然

column1: For example, in the early 1970s, two employees of the company 3M each had a problem: Spencer Silver had a product – a glue which was only slightly sticky – and no use for it, while his colleague Art Fry was trying to figure out how to affix temporary bookmarks in his hymn book without damaging its pages.
column2: 例如，20世纪70年代初，3M公司的两名员工各有一个难题：斯宾塞·西尔弗研制了一种黏性很弱的胶，却找不到用处；同事阿特·弗赖则在琢磨，怎样把临时书签固定在赞美诗集里，又不损伤书页。
column6: no use for it|找不到它的用途

column1: The solution to both these problems was the invention of the brilliantly simple yet phenomenally successful Post-It note.
column2: 解决这两个难题的，是便利贴的发明。它巧妙而简单，却获得了极大的成功。

column1: Such examples give lie to the claim that ingenious, designing minds are responsible for human creativity and invention.
column2: 这些例子表明，认为人类的创造和发明全靠天才有意设计的说法并不成立。

column1: Far more banal and mechanical forces may be at work; forces that are fundamentally connected to the laws of science.
column2: 在起作用的，可能是一些远为平常、机械的力量；这些力量从根本上与科学规律相连。

column1: The notions of insight, creativity and genius are often invoked, but they remain vague and of doubtful scientific utility, especially when one considers the diverse and enduring contributions of individuals such as Plato, Leonardo da Vinci, Shakespeare, Beethoven, Galileo, Newton, Kepler, Curie, Pasteur and Edison.
column2: 人们常用灵感、创造力和天才这些概念来解释问题，但它们含义模糊，科学上的用处也值得怀疑。考虑到众多人物各不相同、影响深远的贡献，这一点尤其明显，例如柏拉图、列奥纳多·达·芬奇、莎士比亚、贝多芬、伽利略、牛顿、开普勒、居里、巴斯德和爱迪生。

column1: These notions merely label rather than explain the evolution of human innovations.
column2: 这些概念只是给人类创新的演化贴上了标签，并没有解释它是如何发生的。

column1: We need another approach, and there is a promising candidate.
column2: 我们需要另一种思路，而眼下已有一个很有希望的选择。

column1: The Law of Effect was advanced by psychologist Edward Thorndike in 1898, some 40 years after Charles Darwin published his groundbreaking work on biological evolution, On the Origin of Species.
column2: 心理学家爱德华·桑代克于1898年提出了效果律，距查尔斯·达尔文出版其开创性的生物演化著作《物种起源》已有约四十年。
column10: On the Origin of Species|《物种起源》

column1: This simple law holds that organisms tend to repeat successful behaviors and to refrain from performing unsuccessful ones.
column2: 这条简单的定律认为，生物体倾向于重复成功的行为，并避免重复不成功的行为。

column1: Just like Darwin’s Law of Natural Selection, the Law of Effect involves an entirely mechanical process of variation and selection, without any end objective in sight.
column2: 与达尔文的自然选择定律一样，效果律涉及一个完全机械的变异和选择过程，并没有预先设定的最终目标。
column3: Law of Natural Selection|自然选择定律

column1: Of course, the origin of human innovation demands much further study.
column2: 当然，人类创新的起源还有待大量进一步研究。

column1: In particular, the provenance of the raw material on which the Law of Effect operates is not as clearly known as that of the genetic mutations on which the Law of Natural Selection operates.
column2: 尤其是，效果律所作用的原材料究竟来自哪里，这一点还没有自然选择定律所作用的基因突变的来源那么清楚。
column9: Law of Natural Selection|自然选择定律

column1: The generation of novel ideas and behaviors may not be entirely random, but constrained by prior successes and failures – of the current individual (such as Bohr) or of predecessors (such as Nicholson).
column2: 新想法和新行为的产生也许并非完全随机，而是受先前成败的制约；这些成败可能是当事人（如玻尔）自己的，也可能来自前人（如尼科尔森）。

column1: The time seems right for abandoning the naive notions of intelligent design and genius, and for scientifically exploring the true origins of creative behavior.
column2: 现在似乎正是时候：摒弃“聪明人有意设计”和天才创造这些过于简单的观念，用科学方法探索创造性行为的真正起源。
column4: naive|adj. 过于简单的；天真的
column6: intelligent design|有智慧者的有意设计
